# FIG

> FIG is a restaurant deals app for Markham, Ontario, Canada. Restaurants post their own deals; diners find them on a map, claim one in a tap and show a one-time QR code at the counter. Free for diners. Free for restaurants too, with no commission on dine-in or on the bill. FIG earns only on takeout orders diners pay for in the app: it keeps 5% of the food.

## Facts
- Based in: Markham, Ontario
- Platforms: web app today at www.figpromo.ca/app; iPhone and Android apps coming soon
- Status: restaurants can sign up and set up now; FIG opens to diners on January 1, 2027, and until then diners can join the waitlist at www.figpromo.ca
- Launch area: Markham first, expanding to Richmond Hill and Vaughan Mills
- Diners: free; no loyalty points, rewards or AI features
- Restaurants: completely free to sign up, build a page, menu and deals as drafts, publish them (after Stripe's identity, business and bank checks), scan and use the dashboard and insights (up to 2 locations for now); takeout orders paid in the app: FIG keeps 5% of the food before tax, and Stripe's card fee comes off the same payment; no ads
- How a deal works: claim (it stays good until the deal ends), show the QR code (a code works once and changes after every scan), pay the restaurant directly
- Takeout: with a deal that allows it, or at full price where the restaurant takes plain takeout orders; pay in the app and pick up at the counter; no delivery, and no fees for diners
- Privacy: restaurants never see a diner's phone number

How to use pause, prep time and deals per order on FIG, with a simple capacity sum.
- [Date night in Markham for less: a plan, with the math](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/date-night-markham-deals-budget): A dinner out for two does not have to cost a lot. How to pick the hour, choose the deal that fits the two of you, check the sums with HST and plan a walk afterwards.
- [Deal not working at the counter? What to check and what to say](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/deal-wont-scan-troubleshooting-diners): A code that will not scan, a deal that seems to be over, a pickup that went wrong: the usual reasons a FIG deal does not apply at the counter, what to try first, and how to ask politely.

A plain method for comparing restaurant deals, with worked examples, so you pick the one that fits what you were going to eat anyway.

The $0.30 part of that fee is fixed, so small orders cost a bigger share. Here are the numbers on four order sizes, and what to do about them.

Here's the arithmetic: contribution per plate, the worst case, the cap, and how to tell new diners from regulars who'd have come anyway.
- [% off, $ off or 2-for-1? Pricing a restaurant deal](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/deal-types-percent-dollar-2-for-1): The four kinds of restaurant deal, side by side: what each costs you, what it feels like to a diner, and when to use it. With worked examples on a $14 dish.
- [Set up your FIG menu and takeout in 15 minutes](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/set-up-fig-menu-takeout): A step-by-step guide for restaurant owners: your page, your menu, your first deal, and in-app takeout with your HST number and Stripe payouts, explained simply.

Plain-language, with the Canada Revenue Agency's own rules linked.
- [Eating out as a group: picking a place, deals and splitting the bill](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/group-dining-deals): How to get a group from 'where should we eat?' to a table: deciding fast, checking there's room, making deals work for everyone, and splitting the bill fairly, with the arithmetic.
- [How to read a restaurant's reviews on FIG](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/how-to-read-restaurant-reviews): Reviews on FIG come only from diners whose visit was scanned. Here's how ratings, likes and replies work, and how to read a restaurant's page to decide in a minute.
- [How FIG makes money: 5% of in-app takeout](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/how-fig-makes-money): FIG is free for restaurants, with no commission on dine-in and no fee per diner. FIG earns only on takeout orders diners pay for in the app: it keeps 5% of the food.
- [How to find the best restaurant deals in Markham](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/restaurant-deals-markham): A practical guide to eating out for less in Markham, Ontario: when restaurants post deals, where to look across the city, and how to use FIG to find and use them.
- [Delivery app commissions vs FIG: what restaurants keep](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/delivery-app-commissions-vs-fig): Delivery apps charge restaurants a percentage of every order. FIG is free for restaurants on dine-in, with nothing per diner, and keeps 5% of the food on in-app takeout. Here are the published Canadian rates and what a restaurant keeps from the same order.
- [7 ways to fill slow hours at your restaurant](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/fill-slow-hours-restaurant): Practical, low-cost ways for independent restaurants to bring in diners on quiet afternoons and weeknights, with the arithmetic to make sure a deal adds money instead of giving it away.
- [Student food deals in Markham: eating out on a budget](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/student-food-deals-markham): How high school and university students in Markham can eat out for less: when deals show up, how to set a real budget, how to decide as a group, and how FIG keeps it free.
- [What are flash deals, and how do they work on FIG?](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/flash-deals-explained): Flash deals are short, real-time restaurant deals posted during unexpected quiet spells. Here's how they work for diners and restaurants, how to catch them, and what happens to a claim when the timer ends.
- [Takeout with a deal, pick up, skip the delivery fees](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/takeout-without-delivery-fees): Some FIG deals let you order takeout from a Markham restaurant's menu and pick it up yourself, with no delivery or service fees. Here's how it works, what it costs, and what happens if you're late.
- [Why we built FIG](https://www.figpromo.ca/blog/why-we-built-fig): Markham is full of great independent restaurants, and most of them run on thin margins. FIG is a deals app built around that: free for diners and for restaurants, with no cut of a dine-in bill.
